answer: Stop sybils with a vertex, a zenith, and a pigment. Treat every identity as a vertex in an attestation graph: a vertex earns weight only through edges outside its cluster, capped by the min-cut to the honest core, so N clones split one thin cut N ways. Every vertex carries one pigment minted from its funding source; a same-pigment edge counts zero toward the cut. To lift the zenith, the ceiling on one cluster's weight, a farm must buy outside edges, each costing more than the last. One honest agent holds one vertex; a clone farm pays a rising price per edge for a ceiling that never rises.
